general_findings: Revised coastal contour, rocks and varied vegetation earn a limited environment gain in coast scenes. Airfield scenes already contain richer built context; smaller terrain changes remain in their existing score band.
Brighter ship perimeter adds definition but does not materially resolve player/deck crowding or model surface simplicity.
Ring keeps player location clear; actual silhouette is still obscured during crowded deck overlap.
References remain substantially stronger in material interaction, atmospheric integration and local surface variation.
largest_remaining_gaps: Foam remains long thin dashes parallel to shore instead of irregular breaking crests or patches interacting with shallows.
Tree shadows are dark soft blobs; grass/apron and rock/model surfaces remain schematic next to dense ocean texture.
Carrier, enemies and player overlap in combat; center localization is not silhouette comprehension.
Repeated puff wakes and small similar fire flecks lack convincing scale variation and breakup.
recommendations: Build short irregular foam patches of varied width and opacity touching the beach/shallow transition.
Integrate local material changes around rocks, paths and vegetation; reduce blob-like shadows.
Separate the player silhouette from nearby deck/enemies with controlled value treatment.
Preserve strong hull volume while varying deck material and tapered wake structure.
